clue.text: Red River said to start in Dakota

indicators.note: said signals that the river's name is taken as spoken, so only its sound is used

parts.note: the Rubicon is the river in Italy that Caesar crossed

indicators.note: to start in points to the opening letter of the word Dakota

explanation.surface: A red river apparently has its source in the American state of Dakota.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red River' tempts as one name (a real US river); split it. Said aloud, RUBICON can pass for RUBICUN, and the first letter of Dakota supplies the final D.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubicund describes a ruddy, healthy-looking complexion, a synonym for red-faced.

clue.text: Dislike being enthralled again?

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
sent is slang for enraptured or carried away, as by music

explanation.surface: A question whether disliking something amounts to being captivated a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE-SENT, enthralled again; 'being' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel bitter displeasure towards it, a synonym for dislike.

clue.text: Flag conveying rude signal from bridge

parts.note: blue means smutty or rude, as in blue jokes
in the card game bridge, a peter is a signal made by playing a high card then a low one

explanation.surface: A banner carrying an obscene gesture flown from a ship's bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' suggests a ship, matching the flag; it is the card game, where a high-low play is called a peter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Blue Peter is the blue-and-white naval signal flag hoisted when a ship is about to sail.

clue.text: Ship — one harbouring a disease

definitions.meaning: a person who hosts an infection and can pass it on without being ill

explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft carrier is a type of vessel, and a person passing on an infection while symptom-free is its vector.

clue.text: Former land of one's birth

definitions.meaning: ... was a South African province, now KwaZulu-...
relating to birth, as in antenatal

explanation.definitionFit: Natal was a historic South African province, and the adjective natal relates to being born.

clue.text: Insect infesting large cat is shed

indicators.note: insects infesting something get inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: Leo is the lion, as in the zodiac sign
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: An insect has got into a big cat, which is cast off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' reads as a verb (the cat sheds its fur) but is the noun for a hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple outbuilding propped against a wall, a kind of hut.

clue.text: It's improved, provided one keeps two journalists apart

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so one piece goes within another
apart says the two journalists are split by what goes between them
two asks for the same journalist abbreviation written twice

parts.note: ED is the standard abbreviation for an editor, a journalist
if means provided, as in on condition that
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Something improved, on condition that one person separates two reporters.
explanation.walkthrough: IF and I sit between two EDs; 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Edified means morally or intellectually uplifted, so bettered.

clue.text: Henry employed in pleasant and suitable job

indicators.note: employed in means set to work inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: nice means pleasant
H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry has been taken on in an agreeable and fitting position.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry is the SI unit of inductance, abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a role or position perfectly suited to someone.

clue.text: Remove it in exchange for extra pay

indicators.note: in exchange suggests the letters swap places, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Taking something away in return for additional wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in exchange' rearranges REMOVEIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtime is the additional wages paid for hours beyond the normal shift.

clue.text: A number of words pronounced by judge

definitions.meaning: a grammatical unit made of words
a punishment declared by a court

explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical unit is a string of words, and a judge passes a punishment of that name in court.

clue.text: Rewrite Chequers article — you can't do it

indicators.note: rewrite asks for the letters to be written again in another order

explanation.surface: Advice that redrafting an article about the Prime Minister's country house is impossible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rewrite' rearranges the fifteen letters of CHEQUERS and ARTICLE; Chequers is the British Prime Minister's country residence.
explanation.definitionFit: Constructing a circle's equal-area square with ruler and compass is proven impossible, so the phrase means attempting the unachievable.

clue.text: Muddling up Latin for wedding

definitions.note: an adjective phrase, matching the adjective answer

indicators.note: muddling means jumbling, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Confusing Latin words when preparing for a marriage ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muddling' rearranges UPLATIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuptial means relating to marriage, as in nuptial vows.

clue.text: Fish-spear I had put in the river …

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the Trent is a major English river
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone placed a fishing harpoon in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trent is a major river of the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A trident is a three-pronged spear, traditionally used for catching fish.

clue.text: … a way to encourage fish

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
urge on means to encourage

explanation.surface: Continuing the river scene: a method of spurring on the fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to the previous clue's river scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is a large fish prized for caviar.

clue.text: Delicacy's needed in standing up to Miss Darling

annotationWithheld.why: Delicacy's needed in standing up to Miss Darling: TO + GRACE reversed gives TOGRACE/ECARGOT, and the extra S can only come from the 's of 'Delicacy's', the definition word, which would then do two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Delicacy's needed in standing up to Miss Darling

clue.text: Sought for gold in recession, and found the stuff …

indicators.note: in recession means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to mine is to dig for gold, so mined means sought for it

explanation.surface: Prospectors dug for gold during an economic slump and struck something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recession' looks economic; it signals reversal, and 'the stuff' is cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a hard-wearing cotton fabric, the material of jeans.

clue.text: I'm right beside you in getting rid of gangster from the community

indicators.note: getting rid of means removing, so a piece is taken out of a word

parts.note: a neighbourhood is a local community
a hood is a hoodlum, a gangster

explanation.surface: Someone close by helps rid the local area of a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a riddle in the first person; the rest takes HOOD from NEIGHBOURHOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living next door is close at hand, the person speaking in the riddle.

clue.text: Bike race — namely, the tour

parts.note: SC is short for scilicet, Latin for namely
a ramble is a leisurely walking tour

explanation.surface: A motorcycle race, that is to say the circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: SC (scilicet) is the Latin abbreviation for 'namely'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scramble is a motorcycle race over rough country.

clue.text: _ a measure of gold is an incentive, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is taken as spoken, by its sound only

parts.note: a carrot is an incentive, as in carrot and stick

explanation.surface: Continuing the gold theme: a unit of purity is an inducement.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading ellipsis continues the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A carat expresses the purity of gold in twenty-fourths.

clue.text: Sort of tile for architectural ornamentation

indicators.note: sort of suggests a variety of the letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kind of tile used to decorate buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' rearranges TILEFOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A trefoil is a three-lobed decorative tracery motif in Gothic architecture.

clue.text: Shut up in Wensleydale, perhaps — just what you want

parts.note: Wensleydale is an English cheese, perhaps marking an example
it means the very thing, as in that's it

explanation.surface: Being confined in a Yorkshire valley is exactly what one desires.
explanation.walkthrough: Wensleydale is both a Yorkshire dale and a crumbly English cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheese it is old slang telling someone to stop or be quiet.

clue.text: Clients want replacement for perforated plate

indicators.note: the letters need replacing in fresh positions, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Customers ask for a substitute for a damaged plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'want replacement' rearranges CLIENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil is a sheet with cut-out holes through which paint is applied.

clue.text: Car, beginning to speed, slows down

parts.note: a brake (shooting brake) is an estate car

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of the word speed

explanation.surface: A car that starts to accelerate then decelerates.
explanation.walkthrough: A brake, or shooting brake, is a British estate car.
explanation.definitionFit: To brake is to reduce speed, so a third-person verb.

clue.text: No pro wants an end to the game before the game's over

indicators.note: before places that piece ahead of the next

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, A
mate (checkmate) ends a chess game

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A non-professional hopes for a finish before the match ends.
explanation.walkthrough: RU (rugby union) is reversed by 'over'.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur plays for love rather than money, the opposite of a professional.

clue.text: Remains of a ship rent by explosive

indicators.note: rent by means torn apart by, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: SS is steamship
HE is high explosive

explanation.surface: Wreckage of a vessel torn apart by a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' looks like a verb (the ship stays afloat) but is the noun for what is left; 'rent by' signals the split.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashes are what is left after burning, especially cremated remains.

clue.text: Student is less tired

explanation.definitionFit: A first-year undergraduate has this name, and as a comparative adjective it means more invigorated.

clue.text: Jack featured in uplifting fairy tale

indicators.note: featured in means appearing inside, so one piece goes within the other
in a down clue uplifting means read upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: an elf is a fairy
jack is a sailor, abbreviated AB

explanation.surface: A sailor appears in a heart-warming story about the little people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' turns ELF to FLE; Jack (a tar) is AB, able seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: A fable is a short moral story.

clue.text: Not after pirate gold via criminal by any means

parts.note: by means no later than, as in by Friday
Captain Hook is the pirate in Peter Pan
or is gold in heraldry
by means via, as in by road
a crook is a criminal

explanation.surface: Chasing a buccaneer's treasure through a lawbreaker, whatever it takes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not after' gives BY, as in a deadline.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means using whatever method, fair or foul.

clue.text: Simply see about a note

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is placed round another

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see
si is the seventh note of the scale, also te

explanation.surface: Just look round a musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; ELY, a cathedral city, is the crossword's favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Easily means without difficulty, a synonym for simply.

clue.text: Acknowledges possession of some land around lake

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece goes about another

parts.note: a decare is ten ares, a measure of land area

explanation.surface: Someone owns a plot of ground surrounding a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: A decare is a metric land measure; DECARES wraps L.
explanation.definitionFit: At customs you declare goods, admitting that you have them.
